claims_to_fix.statement: CXCL8 is among the most strongly and consistently up-regulated genes in biopsies and has anti-IL-8 antibodies in Phase 2, but it has zero genetic association score, and plasma MR is null (p [gene=CXCL8; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; p=0.289]) with no replication in FinnGen. Its signal reflects neutrophil-driven inflammation rather than causal genetics.

claims_to_fix.statement: JAK2 has a high Open Targets association (second among known UC targets) and approved or clinical inhibitors, but only a small biopsy change. No pQTL or eQTL instrument, so MR is not tested. JAK1 and JAK3 are the clinically used UC JAK targets in the top list.

claims_to_fix.statement: CHI3L1 is one of the strongest, fully replicated up-regulated genes (all cohorts same direction) but has zero genetic association and no drug, so it is a biomarker candidate rather than a genetically supported target.
AQP9 is strongly up-regulated and replicated, with high inflammation specificity, but has no genetic association and no drug, so it is an expression-led biomarker candidate.
